item.title: Palestinian lawmaker accuses Netanyahu of using scapegoating tactics over Arab voter turnout
item.description:
Palestinian lawmaker accuses Netanyahu of using scapegoating tactics over Arab voter turnout

Middle East Eye's James Schneider speaks with Ofer Cassif, a member of the Israeli Knesset, who says that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his allies' claims of foreign interference and voter fraud are typical tactics used by a defeated "dictator".

Cassif added that Netanyahu is resorting to incitement and scapegoating to maintain his grip on power, calling the accusations directed at Arab Palestinian citizens a "racist blood libel".

item.title: Report: US launched strikes on Iran
item.description:
Report: US launched strikes on Iran

The US military is responsible for strikes on Iran, according to The Wall Street Journal citing an unnamed US official. 

The newspaper indicated that the attacks were part of a series of limited operations Washington had "secretly carried out" against the country. 

Earlier, several explosions were heard in southern Iran's  Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz as well as in the coastal city of Bandar Lengeh in Hormozgan province.

The strikes come despite US president Donald Trump's remarks saying he would not launch attacks against Iran after the midterms.

item.title: 'Show courage' and end Netanyahu's government, Tibi urges Israeli opposition leader
item.description:
'Show courage' and end Netanyahu's government, Tibi urges Israeli opposition leader

Speaking to David Hearst, Palestinian lawmaker Ahmad Tibi urged Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to show political courage and work with Arab parties to end Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s rule.

"I hope Eisenkot will be courageous enough to go forward and form a minority government, which will end this government of Netanyahu immediately," Tibi said.

In the latest episode of the David Hearst Podcast, Ahmad Tibi, founder and leader of the Ta’al party, said there was no democratic justification for ruling out cooperation with Palestinian representatives in the Knesset this time around.    

Tibi’s party is part of the Joint List, alongside two other Palestinian-led parties, Hadash and Balad. Together, they won 11 seats. Another Palestinian party, Ra’am, secured eight, giving the two slates a combined 19 seats - a record for Palestinian parties in parliament.  

The results mean that neither a Netanyahu-led nor an Eisenkot-led bloc can secure a 61-seat majority without Palestinian parties.

item.title: Blasts heard in southern Iran
item.description:
Blasts heard in southern Iran

Explosions were heard overnight in southern Iran, according to several local reports. 

The blasts were reported on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz as well as ones heard in the coastal city of Bandar Lengeh in Hormozgan province.

item.title: Netanyahu says he is open to broad Israeli government but insists on leading it
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Monday he was open to talks on forming a broad government but insisted that he should remain prime minister, Anadolu reports. Likud “aspires to form a broad government with our partners and with any party that wishes to do so and does not support terrorism,” Netanyahu said on US social media platform X. “I am open to holding a dialogue on the matter,” he added. Netanyahu claimed that “the public in Israel does not want a government that is dependent on Ra’am and the Joint List,” referring to the two Arab parliamentary lists. “From day one our hand has been extended to establish a broad national government,” he said. item.title: UK defence secretary accuses Iran of ‘bare-faced cheek’ over terrorist labels for British armed forces
item.description: UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting on Monday accused Iran of “bare-faced cheek” after Tehran branded the Royal Navy and Royal Air Force “terrorist organisations,” Anadolu reports. The Iranian move, which also included labelling MI6 a “hostile group,” came in response to the British decision to outlaw support for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). Responding to Tehran’s move during a joint news conference in Berlin with German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius, Streeting said Iran had a record of “state-sponsored terrorism.” “The charge levelled at the Royal Navy and the Royal Air Force by Iran doesn’t really dignify a response,” he said, adding that he was minded to put press clippings of the accusations in his downstairs toilet “as a trophy.” He […]

item.title: Russia expresses ‘deep concern’ over reports of planned new military action against Iran
item.description: Russia on Monday expressed “deep concern” over reports of planned new military action against Iran, Anadolu reports. Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova said the situation surrounding Iran, which she described as having been subjected to unprovoked aggression by the US and Israel, remained “complex.” “The conflict remains unresolved; it resonates with and is intertwined with other crises unfolding across the Middle East,” she said. Zakharova stressed the need to intensify diplomatic efforts to normalize the situation and expressed support for mediators working to advance negotiations. item.title: Tehran engaged in ‘intensive shuttle diplomacy’ through Qatari, Pakistani mediators: Foreign minister
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Monday that Tehran is engaged in intensive diplomatic contacts through Qatari and Pakistani mediators, involving dozens of telephone calls and “intensive shuttle diplomacy,” Anadolu reports. Speaking to Iran’s state news agency IRNA at the conclusion of a visit to Turkmenistan, Araghchi said Tehran had presented a clear plan and conditions for a diplomatic resolution, leaving the next step to Washington. “We have announced our specific conditions and presented our formulated plan; now everything depends on how much political rationality prevails on the American side and whether there is a will to take the wise path of diplomacy or, as in previous instances, to drag the situation toward aggression and military operations,” he said.
